minutes.headline: Select Board agreed to put an override on the warrant and ballot, number undecided; Shady Point deal replaces Lake Shirley transfer.
minutes.summary: A marathon meeting dominated by public comment and a long discussion of a possible FY25 Proposition 2.5 override. The board voted no action on both open-space transfer requests, approved a Kindred Spirits license, a T-ball license, a teen center lease and a DPW appointment, and heard a Personnel committee update on the pay grid. On the override, members were split, but the chair said the board would put an article and ballot question forward with the amount to be set later.

what_happened.line: The board concluded it will put an override article on the warrant and a ballot question forward, with the amount to be set within a week.
The board agreed to advise the town manager that additional revenue or savings be directed to the school department.
The board voted no action on the request to transfer 51 Parmenter Road to the Parks Commission; the vote on the Shirley Reservoir parcel was not audible.
The board approved the teen center lease and sent it to the Boys and Girls Club board; a T-ball license draft and a Kindred Spirits license also passed.
The board agreed by consensus on state earmark priorities: 911 compliance, a police simulator, then cybersecurity.

why_it_matters: A Proposition 2.5 override for FY25 is headed to the warrant and ballot, so residents will likely be asked to vote on a tax increase whose amount has not yet been set.
The board's direction that extra revenue go to the schools bears on how much of the school budget gap an override would have to cover.
watch_next: The override amount, which the chair said would be clarified within a week of this meeting.
The annual town meeting warrant article and ballot question wording for the override.
